thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx & timeout spike observed from gateway -> scheduler (p95 latency and 5xx rate increased). Severity: S2. Affected: hosted inference pool us-west-2.
laura (oncall): paging in. I'm on it. :rotating_light:
mike (sre): on standby, joining. Can you paste the alert link?
laura (oncall): https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/2412345678 - shows 5xx rate up 12% over baseline and gateway timeouts increasing. queue_depth metric for scheduler-batcher trending up rapidly.
jin (runtime): I see a concurrent increase in batch queue length on batcher nodes: batcher-pool-3. KV cache write latency spike too.
laura (oncall): initial customer-impact check: support reports intermittent timeouts for some hosted API customers. Sarah, any escalations?
sarah (support): two customers opened tickets (cust-a, cust-b) reporting 504s, both are high-throughput embedding jobs. Notified account CSMs. We'll draft an update once we have root cause.
dan (eng-plat): tagging in. Any config changes rolled out in the last 30m? I don't see deploys in canary pipeline.
mike (sre): checked deploys - nothing in the last 45m. Autoscaler logs show surge to 100% allocated but new instances not joining fast enough.
ops-alerts-bot: autoscaler: pool scale request queued: +8 nodes, reason: batcher saturating. Provision latency ~6m currently.
laura (oncall): hypothesis: sudden workload spike + slow node provisioning -> head-of-line blocking in scheduler batching queue -> gateway timeouts and upstream 5xx. Plan: 1) divert new incoming low-priority traffic to overflow route 2) temporarily reduce max_batch_size to force smaller batches 3) enable emergency throttle for heavy embedding route.
jin (runtime): can reduce max_batch_size for model-open-ggml-2 in config maps. Will that increase token cost? yes but reduces HOL risk.
mike (sre): I'll flip routing to send non-critical tenants to fallback lightweight instances. Command: `redwood route set --pool hosted-fallback --filter "tenant in (free-tier, non-sla)"` Anyone object?
laura (oncall): go ahead mike. Also create an exception in rate-limiter for internal health-checks.
dan (eng-plat): I'll start a manual scale-up for dedicated spare nodes while autoscaler catches up. `infractl node add --pool batcher-pool-3 --count 4`
jin (runtime): reducing max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for model-open-ggml-2 now. Pushing config: ```kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: batcher-config-model-open-ggml-2
data:
  max_batch_size: "32"
EOF
``` Applying... applied.
mike (sre): routed non-sla traffic to hosted-fallback. `route update succeeded` :thumbsup:
ops-alerts-bot: autoscaler: manual add 4 nodes requested, provisioning started.
laura (oncall): monitor latency and 5xx after these changes. Can people post the key metrics every 2 min? I'll collect for status update.
jin (runtime): KV cache eviction triggered on batcher-pool-3 earlier, that may have led to cold cache misses -> slower handling. Looking at eviction logs: `evict: shard-7 count=1200` — pushing a conservative TTL bump now.
mike (sre): 2 min check: 5xx rate down from 12% -> 7% but still >baseline. p95 latency dropping from 2.1s -> 1.4s. Queue depth decreased by ~40%.
sarah (support): drafting customer update: "We're investigating elevated timeouts and have activated mitigations (traffic reroute, temporary throttles). Some customers may see degraded throughput. We'll follow up." Want to review before posting.
laura (oncall): share the draft please.
sarah (support): posted internal draft in #support-notifications. Short and transparent. cc: ops.
dan (eng-plat): nodes are joining, 3/4 provisioned. Expect full join in ~2m.
jin (runtime): TTL bump for kv cache applied. Also enabling prefix caching for embeddings route which tends to reuse keys.
mike (sre): 5xx down to 4.2% now. p95 ~1.1s. Gateway timeouts reduced significantly. Looks like throttling + smaller batches helped.
laura (oncall): good. Let's keep overflow route and reduced batch until node pool stabilizes for 30m. We'll gradually revert.
jin (runtime): note: reducing batch size increased number of batches processed -> CPU utilization on batcher nodes increased slightly but still under 75%.
laura (oncall): support: please publish a 15-min interim update to affected customers: include ETA for full remediation (60m) and that we activated emergency routing and increased capacity.
sarah (support): published update. customers notified. reactions: :white_check_mark: from CSM on cust-a.
ops-alerts-bot: alert suppressed: severity downgraded to S3 (automated) at 2412346120.
mike (sre): creating an incident ticket in tracker: INC-2412345678 with summary and mitigation steps.
laura (oncall): next steps: write a short post-incident note: root cause hypothesis = sudden high-concurrency embedding workload + slow provisioning + KV cache eviction causing HOL. Action items: faster node warm pool, autoscaler tuning, proactive prefix caching for embeddings, circuit breakers per tenant.
dan (eng-plat): I'll add autoscaler tuning ticket and a runbook update for manual scale path.
jin (runtime): will open a task to improve cache eviction heuristics and add metrics to detect cold-cache storms earlier.
sarah (support): will follow up with customers in 3 hours with status and link to incident ticket.
laura (oncall): wrapping: we leave mitigations in place until 60m stable. If metrics hold, we'll start rollback sequence: revert batch_size -> 64 then remove overflow route. Mike, coordinate rollback.
mike (sre): acknowledged. I'll prepare rollback steps and test on canary first.
laura (oncall): thanks team. Closing live thread; continue updates in INC-2412345678. :pray:
incident-bot: Incident S2 -> transitioned to monitoring at 2412346289.
